title: COPPA children's online privacy rule
why: Products directed at children under thirteen cannot rely on self-asserted consent or ordinary analytics defaults: verifiable parental consent must precede collection, behavioural advertising and unnecessary trackers are prohibited, and a parent must be able to inspect, revoke and erase their child's records at any time.

addRequirements.title: Verifiable parental consent precedes child data collection
addRequirements.statement: When an account or {primary} is created for a child under thirteen, the application shall obtain and record verifiable parental consent before storing or sharing personal information beyond the one-time parent contact needed to request consent.
addRequirements.definition: A child cannot enter persistent personal data until a verified parent or guardian grants consent tied to the operator's direct privacy notice.
addRequirements.failurePath: If parental consent is declined, unverified or does not arrive within the verification window, the pending parent contact and any provisional child state are deleted automatically.
acceptance: Given an unverified child signup, when personal information is submitted, then the application refuses persistence and prompts the parental-consent flow.
Given a pending consent request past its expiry window, when the cleanup job runs, then the parent contact record is purged.
Given a verified consent grant, when the consent record is inspected, then it captures method, notice version, parent identifier and timestamp.

addRequirements.title: Parents can inspect, revoke consent for and erase child records
addRequirements.statement: When a verified parent requests review, consent revocation or deletion of a child's data, the application shall disclose every stored child field, stop further collection immediately and erase the child's personal data across primary storage and processors.
addRequirements.definition: Parental control outlives onboarding: revoking consent halts future collection and deletes existing child data without requiring closure of unrelated sibling accounts.
addRequirements.failurePath: If a downstream processor deletion fails, the application locks the child record from read and collection, queues retried erasure and surfaces the failure to an operator.
acceptance: Given a verified parent, when they request their child's record, then the response returns every personal field collected for that child and no other child's data.
Given a consent revocation, when the child session next attempts a write, then collection is refused immediately.
Given a parental deletion request, when erasure completes, then no personal field for that child remains queryable.

addRequirements.title: Child sessions collect the minimum needed and forbid behavioural tracking
addRequirements.statement: The application shall restrict child data collection to fields required to participate in the {primary} activity and forbid behavioural advertising identifiers, third-party ad pixels or unconsented geolocation on child accounts.
addRequirements.definition: Participation cannot be conditioned on disclosing extra personal data, and persistent identifiers are limited to support for internal operations.
addRequirements.failurePath: If an optional tracker, ad SDK or precise-location field is supplied on a child route, the application strips or rejects it and logs a policy violation.
acceptance: Given a child session, when outbound payloads and rendered pages are inspected, then no third-party advertising tracker or behavioural profile identifier is present.
Given a submission containing extra personal fields or precise geolocation not required by the activity, when validated, then those fields are rejected.
Given a retention policy check, when a child record is no longer needed for the activity, then personal fields are deleted on schedule.

addRequirements.title: Direct notice and child-data third-party operators are inventoried
addRequirements.statement: The application shall publish a direct notice naming every operator or processor that receives child data and refuse outbound child-data calls to any destination absent from the approved inventory.
addRequirements.definition: Parents can see who handles their child's data before consenting, and code enforces the same list.
addRequirements.failurePath: If an unapproved vendor endpoint is configured for a child workflow, the outbound call is refused and logged rather than sent.
acceptance: Given an outbound child-data integration not in the approved operator list, when invoked, then the call is blocked and recorded.
Given a material change to the operator inventory, when published, then affected child accounts require renewed parental consent before new sharing occurs.

addGates.statement: Unverified child collection is refused, behavioural tracking is absent, and parental revocation/erasure is proven by automated tests.
